summary: The worker can now run the Claude coding agent with tightly restricted permissions and a fixed instruction. Community text never reaches it directly, and the behavior is covered by passing tests that use a fake command runner.

assessment.requirements: The adapter, the restricted-permission setup, the shell-free invocation and the mocked-executor tests are all delivered. The agent gets only a fixed prompt that points at the structured task files, so no raw community text is passed.
assessment.business: The worker can now hand structured development tasks to Claude Code safely, which is a step toward turning community ideas into real game changes. This sub-goal adds no player-facing change on its own.
assessment.technical: The adapter calls an injected command runner with a command name and an argument list, never a shell string. It allows only file read/edit tools, blocks shell and web tools, and rejects an empty work directory and a missing runner. Passing tests with a fake runner cover each of these. A remaining risk is that cost tracking always reports zero, and the real command runner is outside this sub-goal.
